newsitem.title: USA: Teen pleads not guilty in Nevada casino killing.
newsitem.headline: Teen pleads not guilty in Nevada casino killing.

text.p: A high school student accused of raping and strangling a 7-year-old girl in a casino restroom pleaded not guilty Tuesday to being a fugitive from Nevada.

In the first step toward extraditing him from California to face charges in Nevada, Jeremy Strohmeyer appeared briefly in a Los Angeles courtroom to enter a plea on the fugitive charge. He was not required to plead on the rape and murder charges.
Judge Michael Kellogg set a June 13 hearing at which Nevada officials must prove Strohmeyer is the suspect they are seeking in the May 25 killing of Sherrice Iverson.
The girl was captured on a security videotape in the Primadonna Casino in Primm, Nevada, entering a ladies restroom followed by a young man authorities believe was Strohmeyer.
The grainy, black-and-white tape showed two men walking near the girl, then showed one of the men following her into the restroom while the other waited outside.
The man came out of the restroom about 25 minutes later, according to a timer on the videotape. The girl's body was later found in a stall in the restroom.
She was killed in the early hours while her father, LeRoy Iverson, gambled in the casino area.

At Tuesday's hearing Strohmeyer's attorney, Leslie Abramson, famed for her defence of convicted murderer Erik Menendez, asked the judge to bar cameras from the courtroom. He refused, but ordered that Abramson and Strohmeyer should not be shown on camera in court.
Strohmeyer, 18, was arrested at his home in Long Beach last Wednesday after another teenager sought in the killing went to police with his parents.
Based on what he told police, an arrest warrant was issued for Strohmeyer. The informant, who was believed to have been in the casino with Strohmeyer, was not arrested or charged.
